boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all ten frozen records in the Gettysburg Campaign [June-July 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates. Middleburg (June 17–19) overlaps Aldie (June 17), and Boonsboro (July 8) lies inside Williamsport's frozen interval (July 6–16); campaign-wide and multi-day totals (for example Stuart's June 17–21 losses and the Count of Paris's campaign estimates) must not be assigned to one engagement or added. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen structured bounds (US 83,289; CS 75,054) are imported source-reported forces-engaged figures and remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads 158,300 total (US 83,289; CS 75,054), with a frozen strength of 158300; the side figures sum to 158,343 (a computation here), which the live field gives. Doubleday says the Confederates had three corps to the Union seven. Lee writes of largely superior numbers on July 1 and of fresh troops in overwhelming numbers.
claims.rationale: The frozen total does not match its own components; the relative statements are not counts. None is adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Lee says his July 3 assault was driven back with heavy loss, and that the severe loss and reduced ammunition made another attempt inadvisable, so he determined to withdraw. Doubleday says more prisoners were taken on Webb's front than twice Webb's brigade, with 6 battle-flags and 1,463 muskets.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 51,000 total (US 23,000; CS 28,000). Doubleday relays the Count of Paris's estimates for the whole campaign: 23,186 Union and 22,728 Confederate. Lee says more than 5,000 prisoners were taken on July 1, and Doubleday that Pettigrew's division reportedly lost 2,000 prisoners on July 3.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The Count of Paris's figures span the whole campaign and are not assigned to this battle.

open_questions: Meade's and the corps reports, Longstreet's and Ewell's reports, the returns and Doubleday's own First Corps role remain deferred; Doubleday is an interested participant.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Doubleday is an interested participant history (he commanded the First Corps at Gettysburg) and Humphreys an interested history by Meade's later chief of staff; both drew on official papers. Lee's and Stuart's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXVII, Part 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
